rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Change in core product definition from free of gluten/soy/corn to free of gluten/soy-protein/corn/all grains except rice, altering the scope of the offered franchise concept.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The allergen-free restriction broadened from gluten/corn/soy to include soy-protein and all grains except rice, changing the scope of approved products and premises.
1 atomic change. New provision gives A&W the option to use the grand opening deposit for its own promotional activities if the franchisee fails to conduct them, a new franchisor discretion.
1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosed $100 per-person food safety training fee, coupled with a new certification requirement, is a clear operational change.

4 atomic changes. New conditional right allows A&W to use the grand opening deposit if the franchisee fails to conduct required promotional activities. Training prerequisite changed from completing Food Safety Training (with optional $100 online module) to mandatory Food Safety Manager certification through specified programs.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Change of mandated digital learning platform provider is an operational change but no cost or burden difference is disclosed.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 12 atomic changes. Material increase in disclosed initial computer system cost range. Material change in training requirement from attendance to formal certification, with different cost structure.

1 atomic change. The 2023 FDD adds a non-exhaustive list of factors A&W may consider when deciding whether to delay or approve additional development, expanding the bases for delay beyond the general unpreparedness standard.
5 atomic changes. Material change in the disclosed profit metric and its definition. New disclosure of an averaging calculation method for P&L categories.
1 atomic change. The 2023 FDD adds a new contract exhibit (POS Service Agreement) to the Item 22 list, a clear operational change in the contracts disclosed, though its terms are not specified.
4 atomic changes. Advertising fee rate doubled from 1% to 2% of Gross Sales. Audit understatement threshold reduced from 2% to 1%, making cost reimbursement more likely.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. The required advertising fund contribution rate increased from 1% to 2% of Gross Sales. The general statement that Fund monies are not used to sell franchises was replaced by a specific disclosure that no Fund contributions were spent on franchise-solicitation advertising in the most recent fiscal year.
1 atomic change. Removal of the exclusive territory grant from the single-location franchise fundamentally changes the territorial economic relationship.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Expands the franchisee's exposure to a shorter 10-day cure period by adding local health code violations as a curable default.

3 atomic changes. The advertising/marketing contribution rate used in the expense illustration increased from 1% to 2% of Gross Sales. Chart 3 switched from dollar actuals to percentages of revenue, changing the unit and comparability of the expense representation.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring of the franchise offering from three PRACTICE variants to FIRM-only. Material change in the scope of franchisor's operational rights from prohibition to limited allowance.

5 atomic changes. The initial franchise fee calculation method changed from fixed flat amounts to a population-based formula, fundamentally restructuring the fee structure. A new non-refundable EBC training fee of $5,000 per EBC is introduced.
6 atomic changes. The Item 6 fee schedule was restructured from three franchise-type tables to a single Firm-franchise table. A new $475 per-EBC quarterly fee was introduced.
6 atomic changes. Equipment cost estimate upper bound increased from $4,000 to $25,000. New conditional EBC/Key Personnel training fee introduced with a $0 to $5,000 range.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Material disclosed revenue amount changed from $50,120.05 to $30,685.87 between consecutive fiscal years.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Changing the franchise type to which a mandatory training program applies is a material operational and economic change. Changing the franchise type to which a mandatory EBC training program applies is a material operational and economic change.

8 atomic changes. The territorial definition changes from a state-level master license territory to a code-defined DDMA. Territory exclusivity changes from explicitly non-exclusive to a limited exclusive Direct Marketing territory.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Removal of a franchisee-type restriction materially expands the right to appoint EBCs. Removing the two-EBC cap is a material change in allowed staffing.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Venue for arbitration changed from initiator-dependent to ACNA-headquarters-based, altering where a franchisor-initiated dispute would be heard. Governing law changed from a fixed Nevada designation to the state of ACNA's headquarters at the time of the dispute, which is currently Nevada but could move.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Introduction of a parent company changes the ownership structure and potential control. New disclosure of directors' and officers' backgrounds provides additional information to prospective franchisees.

4 atomic changes. A $1,000 Application Fee with retention/credit mechanics was removed from Item 5 disclosure. The multi-unit discount is now limited to existing franchisees rather than any awardee of more than one opportunity at a time.

16 atomic changes. Audit cost trigger changed from any underreporting to underreporting over 2% of Gross Revenues, with expanded costs and interest. New $250 fee for replacing a lost or damaged Confidential Operating Manual was introduced.

4 atomic changes. A new program option with a separate, higher initial investment structure is introduced, fundamentally expanding the available franchise model. A new cost category and obligation for permits, licenses and certifications is introduced with a $0-$1,000 estimate.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 15 atomic changes. Converts a stated evaluation obligation into a purely discretionary franchisor option. Creates a new unilateral franchisor right to force franchisees to stop selling products/services.

6 atomic changes. Acceleration is expanded from late payment alone to other defaults, Franchise Agreement breaches, and transfer/expiration/termination events. The explicit addition of the franchisee's own attorney's fees expands the franchisee's default-related financial exposure.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 9 atomic changes. Added franchisor discretion to require additional training and shift the costs to the franchisee. Introduced franchisor authority to specify minimum insurance limits and require additional policies.

12 atomic changes. A new obligation requires the franchisee to absorb the cost of adopting new brands after a merger or acquisition. A new post-merger right permits competing services under other names in or near the franchisee's territory without compensation.

3 atomic changes. IP ownership shifted from the franchisor to its parent with a license-back, restructuring the rights the franchisee relies on. A new contractual assistance obligation is added, giving the franchisor discretion over the support and documents required.
1 atomic change. New credit of public figure expenses against required Local Advertising expenditures is a clear conditional economic offset.
5 atomic changes. Introduces a new program-scope limitation on the financial performance representation. Reporting owner count changed from 53 to 50, a material population change.

5 atomic changes. Introduces a fundamental restructuring of the franchise agreement counterparty for most existing outlets. Introduces an agreement centralizing payment collection and service provision for the affiliate's franchise agreements.

3 atomic changes. The disclosed contract name changes the scope of assigned assets from contact/electronic information to telephone/internet listings and advertisements. The disclosed confidentiality contract is renamed to include non-use and non-competition obligations.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Franchisor changed from a Delaware corporation to a Delaware LLC through a disclosed conversion, a material legal-entity change affecting liability and tax structure. The franchisor's relationship to Falafelshop, Inc changed from wholly owned subsidiary to affiliate, a structural corporate change.
1 atomic change. The 2016 FDD removes both previously disclosed Chapter 7 bankruptcy filings, a clear disclosure-content change with limited direct economic effect.

2 atomic changes. Removal of a conditional 25% refund of the Initial Franchise Fee changes the franchisor's refund obligation and the franchisee's financial risk. Removal of a conditional 50% refund of the Initial Franchise Fee changes the franchisor's refund obligation and the franchisee's financial risk.
2 atomic changes. New conditional fee of $600 per day for overlap caused by delayed opening. New contractual obligation imposing a per-day training fee during delayed opening when staff are onsite.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Removal of a franchisee termination right and 50% refund upon best-efforts site acquisition failure is a material contract right change. Expansion of designated POS system from OnePOS only to OnePOS or Square is a clear operational change.

2 atomic changes. The franchisee's Manual-update duty is materially restated to require consulting the most current version and to limit hard-copy updating to when a hard copy is provided. The dispute-resolution controlling copy is redefined from a headquarters physical copy to a franchisor-maintained version, altering the source of control.

2 atomic changes. Removal of the disclosure of parent audited financial statements from Item 21 is a material change in required financial disclosure. Removal of the disclosed unconditional parent guarantee is a material change in the economic protection available to franchisees.
4 atomic changes. Removal of a specific contract exhibit disclosure from Item 22 is a clear disclosure-method change.

3 atomic changes. Removal of a substantive contract attachment from the disclosed contract package. Introduction of a new contract attachment is a substantive change to the disclosed contract package.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New obligation sets a deadline for ordering the first van relative to training, an operational timing and execution change. New disclosure defines when the first franchise agreement begins, an operational timing and execution change.
2 atomic changes. New material fee for an optional fourth territory. New explicit single-transaction purchase requirement without a comparable old provision.
11 atomic changes. The reference fee for additional territories changed from initial to second Territory Fee. New CMS fee of $400 per month creates a new ongoing obligation.

7 atomic changes. The required minimum monthly grand opening marketing spend doubled from $1,500 to $3,000. The financing requirement changed from mandatory to optional, and outright purchase was added as an option.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Removes the franchisor's exclusive-source status for the previously listed goods, changing the obligation to purchase from the franchisor as the only source. Raises the mandatory minimum uninsured motorist coverage, increasing a required insurance cost.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring: introduction of a new multi-unit development offering. New explicit minimum revenue threshold for eligibility under the introduced development agreement; material financial condition.

3 atomic changes. Introduces a new reduced initial fee amount for development-schedule franchises, a material change in fee structure. Adds franchisor discretion over population database and announces planned database switch, a clear operational change in fee calculation inputs.

5 atomic changes. New conditional reduced Continuing Franchise Fee rate for area developers is a material economic condition change. New indemnification obligation for area developers is a material economic condition change.

7 atomic changes. The entire Item 9 table switches from franchise agreement obligations to area development agreement obligations, fundamentally changing the scope of the disclosure. Introduces a conditional financial incentive with repayment obligation on default, a material economic condition.
5 atomic changes. Adds a new financing option for Development Fee, materially expanding financing availability. Introduces a new down payment obligation for Development Fee financing.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 13 atomic changes. Introduces a new development obligation with specific opening dates and a $500,000 annual revenue threshold for ADA franchisees. Reduces the mandatory meeting attendance from both an annual convention and a regional meeting to either one, easing the franchisee's obligation.

9 atomic changes. Introduces a discretionary path to multi-unit development rights, changing the prior no-option position. Introduces franchisor remedies to reduce or terminate development rights upon default.

2 atomic changes. Material change in the franchisor's discretion standard from 'sole' to 'sole and absolute' discretion, strengthening franchisor control over trademark application approval. Expansion of the prohibition on unauthorized use of Licensed Marks in social media identifiers to include handles and usernames.

2 atomic changes. 2018 introduces a material disclosure of an ongoing lawsuit involving Clockwork IP, a clear disclosure-method change. 2018 modifies the confidentiality agreement signing obligation by adding franchisor discretion to require the form periodically.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. New Area Development Agreement provision grants franchisor right to require execution by individuals and other business entities. Franchisor's right to require execution of Owner's Guaranty expands from individuals to individuals and other business entities.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 12 atomic changes. Introduces transfer conditions for the Area Development Agreement, including a $10,000 transfer fee and requirement to sign then-current agreement for term ending at expiration. Introduces curable default and cross-default provisions for the Area Development Agreement, including a 30-day cure period and franchisor discretion to treat franchise defaults as area development defaults.

5 atomic changes. Net Sales definition was materially expanded to include any other income and sales regardless of authorization or location. The rebate population was narrowed from all BuyMax users with two-year Net Sales to BuyMax members with full-period Net Sales.
1 atomic change. Governance change from franchisor-selected to franchisee-vote FLT membership with franchisor vacancy appointment.

4 atomic changes. A new Area Development Agreement contract type is added to the Item 22 attached-contract list, a material change to the contract package even though its terms are not stated in this item. Georgia is dropped from the states covered by the attached state-specific amendments, a clear scope change in the contract package.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. The incentive is re-targeted from any signed Franchise Agreement to Area Development Agreements for three or more restaurants. The required opening timing for the incentive changes from a 300-day/December 31, 2023 condition to a 30-days-before-scheduled and June 30, 2026 condition.

1 atomic change. The required list of mandatory pre-opening goods from the affiliate was reduced from a broad bundle to only cooking utensils, materially changing the franchisee's purchase obligation.

15 atomic changes. New requirement to name franchisor and affiliates as additional insureds on franchisee insurance policies. New required insurance coverage for liquor liability with specified limits, adding a new franchisee obligation.

17 atomic changes. Area Development Fee low end reduced and minimum business count lowered from 3 to 2. New mandatory fee for on-site opening training and assistance, with different amounts by restaurant concept.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Designated supplier pool for proprietary sauce expanded from sole Bonchon LLC to Bonchon LLC plus seven regional suppliers, materially altering required source obligations. New exclusive beverage sourcing agreement with mandatory participation agreement and conversion obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 15 atomic changes. New optional program with conditional architectural fee liability. New obligation for franchisee to pay for merchandising materials if provided.

2 atomic changes. Removal of a reimbursement obligation is a material change in the economic relationship on trademark compliance costs. Broadening of the franchisor's liability release from 'resulting expenses' to 'other expenses, losses or damages' is a clear operational/contract change.
1 atomic change. The FDD expands the class of persons required to sign the Confidentiality Agreement to include all non-managerial personnel, a material contractual obligation change.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Introduces a new operational staffing obligation requiring at least one Restaurant Manager on duty during all hours of operation. Expands the population required to sign the Confidentiality Agreement to include all non-managerial personnel, materially broadening the confidentiality obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 37 atomic changes. Liquidation added to ADA automatic non-curable termination triggers. New ADA non-curable default ties termination to uncured breaches under any related agreement.
4 atomic changes. New growth rate metric introduced. Addition of a new inclusion/exclusion threshold changes the disclosed population definition.
1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosed interim unaudited financial statement is a clear disclosure-method change in Item 21.

6 atomic changes. A contract exhibit (Acknowledgement Addendum) was removed from the Franchise Agreement package disclosed in Item 22. A new Architect Design Services Agreement was added to the contract list disclosed in Item 22.

4 atomic changes. Introduction of a $600 per person per day cap on Additional Training fee, a material change to the fee obligation. Change in determination of third party charges for Additional Training from franchisor sole discretion to actual amounts, a material fee condition change.

2 atomic changes. A new mandatory retail training cost and attendance requirement is introduced in both investment tables. Disclosed high estimate for three months of additional funds was reduced by $25,000 in both investment tables.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Changes the conference fee from a stated not-to-exceed cap to a current amount that may be increased subject to a 20% cap. Introduces franchisor ownership and control over website domains and digital assets, removing franchisee ownership interest.
1 atomic change. Territory formation criterion changed from population and mileage to population and average household income.

2 atomic changes. Adds a new condition to the existing LEGO trademark use restriction: compliance with applicable LEGO brand guidelines in addition to prior written consent. Adds a clear post-termination cessation of trademark rights; a timing/scope change in the franchise relationship.

5 atomic changes. Material change in gross margin population and inclusion rule, affecting the comparability and interpretation of gross margin statistics. Introduction of a data reliability and inclusion rule that affects how the performance statistics are compiled and disclosed.

3 atomic changes. Disclosed company-owned outlet count at end of fiscal year 2024 was revised from 7 to 6. Disclosed historical franchised outlet count for the same fiscal year (2023) was revised downward by one outlet in the 2026 FDD.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduction of a distinct franchise offering type with a separate rider materially expands the franchise opportunity.
1 atomic change. New pending litigation disclosure added to Item 3; no counterpart in prior year.

5 atomic changes. Material change in initial franchise fee amount for ADA-covered Franchise Agreements, introducing a higher $45,000 fee for 20-year term agreements. New initial franchise fee provision for Non-Traditional Location restaurants.

4 atomic changes. The early-opening benefit now extends reduced royalty rates through month 42 instead of reverting to full incentive rates after 6 months, lowering franchisee royalty burden for qualifying openings. New 1.12% Brand Fund rate for Non-Traditional Locations, about half the 2.25% standard rate, lowers fee burden for that category.
6 atomic changes. New disclosed cost category of up to $15,000 payable to franchisor for opening team expenses. Estimated range for architecture fees increased at both ends.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Introduction of a defined 0.5% of Gross Sales Brand Fund contribution for Non-Traditional Location restaurants; material fee provision. New exemption from advertising Cooperative participation for Non-Traditional Location restaurants.
1 atomic change. Added a new provision stating that the Non-Traditional Rider grants no geographic or territorial protections.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. The disclosed franchise term duration increased from a fixed 10 years to an option of 10 or 20 years, materially altering the contract term. Renewal availability is now conditional on whether the original term is 10 or 20 years, with a new prohibition on renewal for 20-year terms.
1 atomic change. The reporting population inclusion threshold changed from 8 to 13 weeks, altering which outlets are included in the Item 19 financial performance representations.
9 atomic changes. Disclosed fiscal year-end company-owned outlet count increased from 15 to 37. Disclosed company-owned outlets opened increased from 14 to 22.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removes a disclosed franchisor discretion to require franchisees to implement future tested programs, a material reduction in potential obligations. The old disclosure offered an optional PUD Addendum to Legacy Plant Store operators; the new FDD removes that option entirely.

3 atomic changes. The incentive initial franchise fee amount changed from $6,000 to $8,000, a material fee change. The disclosed actual initial fees for the prior-year Satellite incentive changed from a flat $4,000 to a $4,000-$6,000 range.

7 atomic changes. A new $300 per day cap was added to the training fee, materially limiting the franchisor's ability to raise this fee. Control transfer fee for a CD Store franchisee transferee decreased from $5,000 to $4,000.

18 atomic changes. Assumed landlord tenant improvement contribution for the Larger Plant Store decreased by $100,000, increasing the likely franchisee burden. Disclosed Kiosk installation cost estimate increased substantially for the larger Plant Store.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. The refurbishment obligation's possible work scope is expanded to include replacing fixtures and counters, giving the franchisor broader discretion over required work. The enumerated asset list in the definition of Operating Assets is expanded to explicitly include auto-assembly system and Kiosk System, altering the scope of assets that must be bought from approved suppliers.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Adding a second franchise product line (Classy Kitchen & Bath) fundamentally expands the franchise offering. The non-compete restriction is expanded to prohibit competition in product lines, a material restriction on franchisee activity.
14 atomic changes. The initial technology fee increases from $500 to $1,000. The conversion franchise fee schedule and related conversion narrative are absent from the new version.

9 atomic changes. The branding fund cap removed the 4%-of-gross-sales component, leaving only the $1,000-per-month cap. The branding fund fee formula changed from a percentage-of-sales basis to a population-based estimate with a fixed annual cap.
7 atomic changes. The design software license fee increased from $1,000 to $2,500. Initial franchise fee changed from a $10,000-$100,000 range to a fixed $50,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Showroom changed from optional to mandatory, a material operational obligation. Removing the Conversion Franchisee telephone number exception imposes a new operational obligation on conversion franchisees.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Removed the conversion-franchisee exception that limited showroom approval to alterations/new showrooms, expanding franchisor approval over existing showrooms. Required Ordering & Scheduling software fee doubled from $500 to $1,000.

7 atomic changes. Changes the base metric for territory performance thresholds from gross sales to net revenue, which alters the calculation and comparability of minimum and average requirements. Expands the scope of brands/products the franchisor may operate/license and the franchisee may sell/install from Classy Closets only to Classy Closets and CK&B.

1 atomic change. New disclosure of an unregistered common law design mark and associated risk of trademark change and increased expenses is a clear operational/disclosure change with limited direct obligation.

2 atomic changes. Expansion of the scope of copyrighted materials to include CK&B Products alters the franchisee's intellectual property rights and obligations. Expansion of the mandatory product change exception to include CK&B Products increases the franchisor's discretion to require changes without the franchisee's written consent.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Material expansion of the products and brands the franchisee is authorized to sell. Removal of the Conversion Franchisee showroom approval exemption expands franchisor control over existing showrooms.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Introduces a new conditional right for the franchisor to terminate development rights, a material control/trigger change. Changes the basis for calculating royalties on transfer, a clear operational change with unknown direction.
3 atomic changes. Clear disclosure-method change in the performance metric definition. Material disclosure-method change: new GAAP consistency, accuracy assumption, and non-audit statements.

2 atomic changes. The disclosure factually changed from no franchisee confidentiality provisions to at least one such provision, materially affecting prospective franchisee access to incumbent-franchisee information. The projected company-owned outlet count changed from zero to one, a clear operational projection change.
1 atomic change. Change in the confirmation exhibit from sales to net revenue procedures is a clear operational change in the contract documents.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. A new named incentive program is added to the Item 1 disclosure of current incentive programs; terms and amounts are not specified in Item 1.
1 atomic change. Old Item 3 disclosed no franchisor-initiated litigation, while the new Item 3 discloses one pending indemnification claim, a clear disclosure-method/content change.

3 atomic changes. The absolute calendar cap on opening was removed from the Growth Incentive eligibility condition, leaving only the 18-month opening window. The signing deadline for the Growth Incentive eligibility was extended by about one year.

4 atomic changes. New franchisor discretion to require contribution to a controlled advertising collective when no cooperative exists is a material potential obligation. Advertising requirement was reorganized from a flat 4.5% expenditure row to a Local Advertising Fee equal to the difference between the NPF rate and 4.5%, changing the calculation method.
20 atomic changes. Conversion building estimate changed from fixed amount to lower range. Conversion equipment estimate changed from fixed amount to lower range.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Material decrease in the range of required cooperative advertising contribution rates. Introduces a new conditional obligation for franchisees to spend up to 4.5% of Net Sales monthly on local advertising if NPF and co-op contributions fall short.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Adds a new transferee obligation to remodel as a condition for franchisor approval of transfer, a material economic condition.
4 atomic changes. The Checkers Table B cohort window and exclusion description changed. The gross margin disclosure sample shrank from 7 to 2 company-owned restaurants and the cohort window changed.

8 atomic changes. Restatement of a disclosed outlet count for the same fiscal year, affecting the reported end-of-year figure. Restatement of a disclosed outlet count for the same fiscal year, affecting the reported start-of-year figure.
1 atomic change. Clear disclosure-method change: removal of unaudited interim financial statements from Item 21 Exhibit H; no fee or obligation is affected.
1 atomic change. Removal of disclosure of pending trademark registration status and associated serial/filing data constitutes a clear disclosure-method change.
1 atomic change. New disclosure statement in Item 20 about potential disclosure of franchisee contact information to other buyers; an operational disclosure-method change.
1 atomic change. The fiscal year end changed from June 30 to December 31, a timing/disclosure change in Item 21.

2 atomic changes. Introduction of a one-time $300 email set up fee is a material new fee. Change from no training to 5 hours of onboarding training for transferee is a clear operational change in transfer support.

3 atomic changes. Lower bound of the disclosed initial inventory cost range increased from $0 to $150 while the upper bound stayed at $200. Lower bound of the disclosed office equipment and supplies cost range increased from $0 to $400 while the upper bound stayed at $2,500.
1 atomic change. Added Table 1A disclosing 2023 partial-year company-owned outlet count as of October 1, 2023.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Minimum required guest rooms reduced from 38 to 35, a clear operational requirement change.

2 atomic changes. The disclosed maximum discretionary Construction Review Fee increased from $10,000 to $20,000, a material change in potential fee exposure. The mandatory Property Management System software/installation fee increased from $7,000 to $15,000, a material fee increase.
15 atomic changes. Construction review fee maximum increased from $10,000 to $20,000. Contactless fee changed from a one-time $0-$500 amount to a $0-$4.00 per room per month recurring fee.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Material increase in the maximum Construction Review Fee that franchisor may charge. Material increase in the required cyber liability and data breach insurance coverage from $100,000 to $500,000.
3 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring of franchisor ownership through acquisition by Bright Horizons. Clear change in the financial officer role from CFO to Director of Finance.

10 atomic changes. The required local marketing expenditure rate doubles from 1% to 2%, a material fee increase. The per-person manager training fee decreases from $495 to $99, a material fee reduction.
1 atomic change. Down payment required for franchisor-financed additional territories rose from 20% to 50% of the initial fee(s), a material financing-condition change.

3 atomic changes. The new FDD introduces explicit third-party discretion over referral/job allocation, a clear operational disclosure change. The new FDD introduces an explicit disclaimer against any minimum referral guarantee, a material expectation-limiting disclosure.

3 atomic changes. New contractual restriction on franchisee's use of Marks in employee-related documents is a material obligation/control change. New disclosure of the absence of federal registration for the principal trademark and associated risks.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The choice-of-forum exception changed from an Exhibit E carve-out to a state-law qualifier, altering the disclosed scope of the forum-selection clause.

6 atomic changes. Changing the required outlet definition from a learning center with 5 tutoring stations to a Community Location without that requirement materially alters the performance representation population and the offered business model. The core Section 1 disclosure changed from price ranges and cost tables based on multiple franchised businesses to a single location's average rates and margins.
1 atomic change. Change from present to past tense and 'then-affiliate' indicates a change in the ownership/affiliation status of company-owned outlets.
1 atomic change. A new disclosure method/content is added to Item 21 financial statements; clear change but not a fee or operational obligation.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Narrowed the scope of PDN services that may be authorized (from 'private duty nursing services' to 'certain' services) and added specific-service prior approval and RN qualification requirements, tightening franchisor control. Disclosure of a European affiliate offering franchises was removed; the franchisor's affiliate network described to prospective franchisees changed.
2 atomic changes. Addition of a pending litigation disclosure is a clear Item 3 disclosure change, not a fee or obligation change.

10 atomic changes. A new incentive program with reimbursement, eligibility, and repayment terms was introduced in Item 5. A new six-month duration for the monthly marketing reimbursement was introduced.

5 atomic changes. The disclosed policy shifts from charging no fee for mandatory training to allowing a fee, increasing potential training costs. The disclosed royalty accrual start changes from the fifth full month to the Start Date, materially advancing the royalty obligation.

4 atomic changes. New prohibition on shared office space imposes a new operational restriction on franchisee office premises. Franchisor changed from not requiring to requiring a professional licensure consultant or attorney, imposing a new obligation on franchisees.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduces a new mandatory purchase from a designated supplier, a material obligation change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 21 atomic changes. The NBF was changed from a terminable, indefinite fund to one with a scheduled termination date of December 31, 2026, fundamentally restructuring the advertising fund arrangement. A new compliance obligation was introduced requiring PHI systems to meet detailed HIPAA and NIST security standards.

4 atomic changes. Material change in the minimum population required to establish a Territory, lowering the floor from 220,000 to 200,000. Clear operational change extending existing office requirements and closure-notice obligations to a new type of location (second Offices).

3 atomic changes. Introduction of a new, materially different financial performance representation (unaudited PMG data) that expands the scope of Item 19 disclosures. Clear change in the disclosed sample size for the historical performance table, reflecting a different reporting period and outlet universe.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The 2018 text adds an eligibility qualifier and an express exclusion of CPR Dual Branded Franchisees from a disclosed marketing support service.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Addition of a state-law override qualifier to an existing choice of law provision; modifies enforceability scope. Addition of a state-law override qualifier to an existing dispute resolution provision; modifies enforceability scope.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Material change in the identity of the contracting franchisor under existing franchise and area development agreements.

4 atomic changes. Introduction of a material pending securities derivative lawsuit against parent/affiliate is a substantive litigation-risk disclosure change. Introduction of a material pending securities class action against parent/affiliate is a substantive litigation-risk disclosure change.

3 atomic changes. Removal of a conditional waiver changes the disclosed fee obligation for Non-Traditional Studio franchisees. The pre-opening Technology Fee rate is reduced from $715 to $250 per month, a material fee change.

2 atomic changes. Late fee selection rule flips from greater-of to lesser-of, reducing the maximum rate. New fee obligation introduced in 2024, payable to an Approved Supplier that may be the franchisor or affiliate.
11 atomic changes. The estimated leasehold improvement range increased substantially. The retail kit payment mechanism changed to an online-store credit and added a 6-month use requirement.

3 atomic changes. The disclosed range of amount financed for the remaining third-party providers decreased from $177,000-$180,000 to $141,000-$154,000. The disclosed Navitas interest rate increased from 8.9% to 9%.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. New disclosed annual Music Licensing Fee range of $1,050-$2,050 represents a new ongoing cost. Disclosed current monthly software fee increased from $185 to $195, a material fee change.
1 atomic change. Removal of a substantive territorial-rights disclosure for non-traditional studios represents a disclosure-method change with economic implications.
1 atomic change. Adds an exclusion to the definition of Confidential Information, narrowing the scope of confidential data and reducing franchisee confidentiality obligations.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of explicit franchisor discretion to set terms and conditions of the reciprocity program, a control shift.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 17 atomic changes. Changes cross-default trigger from any default under other agreements to a failure to cure such a default. Expands the during-term non-compete restriction from the franchisee alone to franchisee and Restricted Parties.

6 atomic changes. A new financial performance representation for average revenue mix was added. The data-collection method underlying every Item 19 chart changed, affecting the reliability and comparability of the representations.

2 atomic changes. Old Item 21 disclosed only an audited consolidated opening balance sheet; new Item 21 discloses a full set of audited financial statements including balance sheet, operations, equity, and cash flows. The financial reporting date changed from an opening balance sheet as of March 15, 2023 to financial statements for the period March 6 through December 31, 2023.
1 atomic change. Removal of a specific disclosed contract exhibit from the Item 22 list is a clear operational change in the disclosure of contracts.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Clear operational change in the description of DPD's product and software licensing scope.
1 atomic change. The group of pending derivative lawsuits expands from three to five, adding two new cases with new allegations.
1 atomic change. Lower bound of estimated total pre-opening payments for a Traditional Store increased from $88,950 to $117,950, while upper bound unchanged.
13 atomic changes. Annual software enhancement fee increased from $780.26 to $819.25 per store per year, a material fee change. Carryout Tracker Bundle fee increased from $347.08 to $440.87.

6 atomic changes. The lower bound of the estimated 3 Month's Rent cost for a Traditional Store increased from $3,000 to $6,000. The lower bound of the estimated furniture, fixtures and equipment cost for a Traditional Store increased from $81,000 to $105,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Per-transaction online ordering fee increased from $0.375 to $0.385, a material fee change. New agreement enabling franchisee orders through Door Dash constitutes an operational change.
4 atomic changes. Disclosed year-end development agreement stock increased by 33. The sponsored advisory group list no longer includes the Domino's Technical Advisory Board.

2 atomic changes. The franchisor removed the exceptions from its employee-authorization clause, so employees may no longer rely on the Item 19 or supplemental information to make representations. The franchisor removed the Item 19 exception from its no-representation policy, consistent with the removal of the performance table.

6 atomic changes. Eligibility for the reduced initial fee changed from third or subsequent to second or subsequent agreements, materially altering which franchisees may pay the reduced fee. New mandatory minimum initial marketing expenditure of $15,000 is introduced.
1 atomic change. Changes a discretionary franchisor option to a mandatory inclusion in extension documents, affecting franchisee obligations.

2 atomic changes. New conditional initial franchise fee tier of $24,900 for second or subsequent agreements, a material fee change. The estimated Additional Funds range for the first three months decreased from $20,200-$28,500 to $9,900-$25,600.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Disclosed estimate of required-purchase cost as a share of establishment cost increased from 83-88% to 88-91%. Disclosed estimate of required-purchase cost as a share of operating cost changed from 9-13% to 10-12%.
1 atomic change. Disclosure cross-reference removes Item 20 from the indemnification row; this is a disclosure-method change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. A recurring staffing obligation is removed from the training requirements. Franchisor access to franchisee computer systems is expanded from direct to direct and independent.
1 atomic change. Modification of relocation consent standard adds 'not unreasonably withhold,' limiting franchisor discretion over a franchisee's ability to relocate.
1 atomic change. New unconditional franchisee obligation to assist in protecting trademarks; modest but operational.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Changes the dispute-resolution mechanism by carving out certain claims from mandatory arbitration. Adds a new post-termination obligation on the franchisee.
1 atomic change. The Table 5 total for signed but unopened agreements rose from 0 to 1.
9 atomic changes. Material increase in the standard Area Representative Fee from $375,000 to $395,000. Increase in the CRM Setup Fee from $1,000 to $1,250.
4 atomic changes. A new recurring fee was introduced for the Fast Track training program. The Franchisee Training Program initial training fee increased by $1,000.
7 atomic changes. Estimated three-month additional funds range increased at both endpoints. Required lump-sum fee increased by $20,000.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Material fee increase of $250 in the CRM system setup fee. Material fee increase of $1,000 in the Franchisee Training Program fee.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New franchisor option to purchase business or 100% ownership interests materially shifts control; disclosed as a right exercisable from the 3rd anniversary.
1 atomic change. Principal mark removed from Item 13 trademark registration list; substantive disclosure change.
1 atomic change. The 2017 FDD omits the numeric totals from the Sweets From Heaven projected openings table that were present in the 2016 FDD.
1 atomic change. The person holding the President position changed from John Dring to Matthew Coleman, a clear operational change in franchisor management.

4 atomic changes. Removal of the $1,200 per person 7-day training fee while retaining the $800 per day off-site fee. Removal of the statement that initial training for the first 2 people is provided at no additional charge.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Quickbooks Pro was added as a required software component for the store information system.

3 atomic changes. Narrowing the permitted trade/home show sales area from DMA to Territory restricts the franchisee's sales venues and enhances franchisor control. Removal of a procedural priority rule for trade/show approvals increases franchisor discretion over approvals.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removal of a permission that owners need not participate personally is a clear operational disclosure change. Change from a recommendation to a direct requirement clarifies the obligation's binding status.
1 atomic change. Disclosure-method change: previously excluded stores now included in the affiliate-owned reporting universe.
1 atomic change. Removal of a contract exhibit from the Item 22 disclosure list; the economic significance is not determinable from the list alone.

1 atomic change. The National Advertising Fund contribution rate changed from a flat 2% of total net sales to a location-dependent rate of 2% for shopping center/mall stores and 3% for other stores, materially increasing the fee for non-mall stores.
12 atomic changes. Satellite architectural fees estimate increased from $1,500-$6,750 to $7,500-$10,750. Satellite kiosk structure estimate increased from $30,000-$60,000 to $55,000-$80,000.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Operations manual changed from loaned with a $21 fee to a purchase obligation. Executive training program was removed from the training requirements.

12 atomic changes. The outlet classification structure changed materially, removing Kiosk and Food Court categories and splitting In-Line into Mall and Off Mall, which affects comparability of all breakdown statistics. The new Item 19 tables no longer disclose the total net sales statistic, changing the financial performance representation.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New pending litigation against parent/affiliate disclosed; material disclosure change.
6 atomic changes. Fee changed from fixed $6,000 to a discretionary cap of $6,000. New mandatory attendance requirement and fee for new construction franchisees.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 9 atomic changes. A new contractual right allows the franchisor to increase any fixed-dollar fee by up to 10% annually, cumulatively, with a CPI override. The trigger condition broadens from a lower publicly available Internet rate to any lower rate, expanding franchisee exposure to the fee.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. A new flat initial fee of $1,499 payable to franchisor is introduced. A new $1,500 fee to franchisor/affiliate is introduced within the technology systems note.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New required purchase obligation from an Approved Supplier for a specific technology system expands the scope of required purchases. New restriction that only one Approved Supplier exists for Wyndham Gateway limits franchisee sourcing options.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. A new one-time 10% acceleration fee on the unamortized balance was introduced for early termination or transfer of a Development Incentive. A comfort letter ('Three Party Agreement') was added as an available third-party financing facilitation document.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Changes the franchisor's installation service from none to installation of a Wyndham Gateway device. Changes the guest-satisfaction trigger for remedial training from a specific numeric threshold to a discretionary 'failing' definition.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Changes a promised assigned territory and mandatory negotiation to a discretionary, request-based negotiation. Changes relocation from a permitted application process to a general prohibition.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. The addition of franchisees' employees to the list of eligible individuals expands the franchisee's mandatory discount-lodging obligation. Expansion of the Best Rate Guarantee prohibition from publicly available channels to any channel materially broadens the franchisee's pricing restriction.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Removal of a franchisee termination right is a material loss of flexibility and control. Removal of a franchisor option to extend the term to 25 years eliminates a potential franchisee benefit tied to SBA lending.

rows.company: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham; Hawthorn Suites Hotels; Hawthorn Suites
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The exhibit listing for C-6 changed from one agreement to a different agreement, altering the set of binding franchise contracts.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removal of a disclosed optional regulatory intelligence program from the Core Services list changes the disclosed support-service scope. Removal of a disclosed optional quality-performance platform from the Core Services list changes the disclosed support-service scope.

9 atomic changes. Estimated upper bound for additional funds at Open Locations increased from $25,000 to $40,000. Estimated range for business licenses at UnOpened Locations increased from $350-$2,000 to $500-$3,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Removal of a shipping charge on the initial branding kit is a clear fee change, though the amount is unspecified and likely minor.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Initial orientation duration changed from estimated 1-2.5 hours to maximum 8 hours. Removal of optional no-fee EQUIPP software offer.
1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosed franchisor reservation to grant territorial protection on a case-by-case basis changes the disclosed territorial rights landscape.
4 atomic changes. Removed a risk disclosure about reduced legal protection for pending-application marks. Introduction of three new registered trademarks in the portfolio table.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Removal of specific disclosed incentives (transition investment payment and right of first refusal) replaced with a general statement; material change in potential economic benefits. Introduction of new pilot programs for enterprise ownership and greenfield territories; clear operational change.
6 atomic changes. Removal of veteran scholarship fee waiver program. Change from discretionary to conditional obligation for deposit agreement availability.

17 atomic changes. The training fee for additional attendees increased from at most $1,750 to a base of $2,250 with a $2,700 cap. A new up-to-10% administrative fee on bulk-purchased systems and services was introduced.

10 atomic changes. New conditional financial assurance obligation for institutional franchise owners, with a 3% gross revenue formula or $65,000 greenfield cap and requirement to pay escrow/letter of credit fees. Office requirement changed from conditional leasing to a mandatory dedicated verifiable business address subject to franchisor approval, expanding franchisor control.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Adds franchisor discretion to mandate Care Platform use in specified transactions, materially increasing franchisor control over operations. Introduces an unconditional obligation to use Required Systems, a material addition to franchisee technology requirements.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 12 atomic changes. Separate additional-person and hotel-room fees were bundled into a single Additional Trainee Fee with a cap Training program restructured from many detailed subjects to four broad subject areas

4 atomic changes. The new text removes the disclosed basis for territory reduction or termination based on non-compliance with other provisions, narrowing the stated enforcement trigger. New explicit disclaimer that franchisee will not receive an exclusive territory and may face competition, a clear change in the disclosure of the territory's nature.
1 atomic change. New disclosure of legal risk and potential expense for unregistered marks; clear disclosure-method change.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Adds a new contractual requirement that the franchisee's manager be approved by the franchisor, increasing franchisor control. Introduces a new conditional allowance for a single Operations Manager across up to three contiguous territories, with franchisor approval and reinstatement right.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The catch-all category of Approved Services was revised from 'any other specialized services' to 'specialized services, and other services to older adults', broadening the disclosed scope of services the franchisee may offer.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 10 atomic changes. Forum changed from fixed Douglas County to county of franchisor's headquarters, allowing future venue shifts. Choice of law changed from fixed Nebraska to headquarters-state law, allowing future change if headquarters moves.

4 atomic changes. Removal of the separate Care Platform growth table for businesses using the platform 6-12 months. Change in the eligibility threshold and reference period for Care Platform growth statistics.

4 atomic changes. Introduction of explicit franchisor discretion to dissolve the franchisee advisory council shifts control toward the franchisor. The disclosed FEC meeting schedule was removed from the new FDD.
2 atomic changes. A new contract exhibit form is introduced, but its terms are not disclosed within Item 22.

2 atomic changes. The outright purchase price for a single Fitness Studio increased from $80,000 to $88,000, a material fee change. The outright purchase price for a single Personal Training Studio increased from $33,000 to $44,000, a material fee change.
1 atomic change. Material increase in the disclosed range of potential inspection/testing costs.

5 atomic changes. Material increase in the stated optional IEP purchase price for a Fitness Studio, although the IEP composition also changed. New operational obligation requiring the franchisee to offer at least six free introductory classes and privates weekly, a material change in marketing conduct.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Disclosed affiliate revenue from franchisee sales increased from $224,429 to $246,183.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Recurring franchisee software fee increased by $22 per month (from $103 to $125).

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Clear disclosed increase in the number of US franchised businesses from 49 to 58. Clear removal of an explicit promise that no other initial franchise fee is required.

2 atomic changes. The household threshold triggering the Additional Population Fee increased from 80,000 to 85,000, changing the fee calculation for territories in that range. The mandatory Supplies Package cost decreased from $7,400 to $5,900.
4 atomic changes. Monthly minimum local marketing spend increased from $2,000 to $3,000, though the duration also changed. Technology Fee monthly amount decreased from $275 to $268.90.

6 atomic changes. Bookkeeping/software fee estimate changed from a $50-$125 range to a flat $300. Initial-period marketing obligation reclassified from a franchisor discretionary concentration right to a fixed $3,000/month minimum.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Specific Property/Business Interruption minimums removed from the enumerated list, while general property coverage obligation remains.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Member selection shifted from current council self-selection to franchisor selection, increasing franchisor control over the advisory council. New franchisor discretion to terminate the Franchise Agreement if the franchisee fails to open within six months.

2 atomic changes. Material increase in the household threshold that triggers the Additional Population Fee from 80,000 to 85,000 owner-occupied households. Material increase in the contractual maximum size of a standard territory from 80,000 to 85,000 owner-occupied households.

3 atomic changes. New disclosure of survey census and response population materially expands Item 19 methodology transparency. The number of owners in the middle and bottom tiers increased from 7 each to 8 each, reflecting a larger Item 19 population.
1 atomic change. The required minimum Grand Opening marketing spend for standard franchisees increased by $2,500, a material increase in initial financial obligation.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Removal of a disclosed reduced royalty rate for conversion franchisees. Removal of a disclosed franchise offering with specific eligibility criteria.

3 atomic changes. Introduction of a litigation disclosure in Item 3, from no litigation to one arbitration case, materially changes the disclosed legal risk profile. Disclosed the resolution of the litigation via settlement, a substantive disclosure of a realized event.

11 atomic changes. Introduction of a disclosed 2% Continuing Royalty rate for the first two years materially changes conversion franchisee economics. Introduction of a disclosed $150 monthly Minimum Royalty term for conversion franchisees is a material new royalty term.

20 atomic changes. The monthly email license fee increased from a flat $6 to a range of $7-$24. A new obligation requiring additional email and software licenses for second or subsequent franchises was introduced.
9 atomic changes. Upper bound of vehicle cost estimate increased more than threefold. New mandatory training attendance requirement for a General Manager added.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 12 atomic changes. New mandatory sole-source services for digital marketing, business platform, and review management. New obligation for franchisee to pay testing/inspection costs and franchisor expenses for alternate supplier approval.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 25 atomic changes. Fixed $25/month license price replaced by franchisor-determined then-current charges. Fixed $6/month email license price replaced by franchisor-determined then-current charges.
1 atomic change. Removal of a promised disclosure element from the pre-signing territory description.
1 atomic change. Introduction of a pending trademark application and disclosure of its unregistered status is a material change to the licensed trademark portfolio and associated risk.

3 atomic changes. New material restriction on franchisee handling of proprietary materials regarding generative AI, requiring franchisor consent. New material contractual restriction on franchisee use of proprietary materials for AI/ML purposes, requiring franchisor consent and shifting control to franchisor.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New contractual requirement that the Operating Principal be approved by the franchisor and hold majority ownership, materially increasing franchisor control over franchisee management structure. Removal of an explicit training obligation for executive, administrative, and marketing personnel, reducing franchisee staffing requirements.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Material new conditional right for franchisor to terminate without cause, shifting control to franchisor. New material termination right for franchisor under Multi-Territory Development Addendum.
1 atomic change. Clear disclosure-method change in how outlets are grouped and how combined locations are treated.
8 atomic changes. The Exhibit F disclosure changed from full last known address to city and state only. The speaking-restriction disclosure changed from 'In some instances' to 'In the last 3 years'.

2 atomic changes. A new contract exhibit is added to the disclosed contract package, a clear disclosure/contract-scope change. A new contract exhibit for multi-territory development is added to the disclosed contract package, a clear disclosure/contract-scope change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Clear operational change in the defined scope of HWR services, listing specific technology-enabled modalities.
